title: AReaL-DTE: Sparse Policy-Weight Transfer for Online Agentic Reinforcement Learning
event_hint: AReaL-DTE: a snapshot-free Delta Transfer Engine for online agentic RL that exploits inference-visible weight sparsity (<2% of BF16 elements change between consecutive policy versions) to make frequent policy-weight synchronization between training and rollout workers sparse across the full data path (construction, layout translation, transfer, application).
problem: Online agentic RL with micro-services separates policy training from rollout generation, making frequent policy-weight synchronization a critical systems overhead. Shared storage connects these services across clusters, but vanilla dense synchronization incurs model-scale construction/transfer/application cost. Existing sparse/checkpoint-oriented approaches (e.g., PULSE) still retain a previous-model checkpoint and materialize complete intermediates to bridge heterogeneous training (Megatron-LM/FSDP) and inference (vLLM/SGLang) layouts (different parameter names, fusion/permutation rules, dtypes, TP/PP/DP/EP layouts). For a policy with N inference-visible elements, a dense refresh constructs, stages, transfers, and applies O(N) values even when the new policy differs at only a small fraction of positions.
mechanism: AReaL-DTE is a snapshot-free Delta Transfer Engine that translates inference-visible weight sparsity into end-to-end efficiency. (1) On-demand reconstruction of overwritten weights by inverting AdamW updates (streaming AdamW inversion), avoiding a persistent historical snapshot. (2) Streams reconstructed and current parameters through converter-aligned BF16 change detection (after aligned conversion to the receiver's layout). (3) Remaps changed elements directly into receiver-local coordinates and delivers receiver-specific updates. Two transports: manifest-committed sparse transfer through shared storage (OSS) across clusters, and a deadlock-safe two-round protocol within a cluster followed by direct scatter-application to inference shards. Preserves layout translation while avoiding a complete-model representation for each refresh; relies on the surrounding control/storage layer for version ordering and consistency. Does not change the rollout schedule, RL algorithm, or consistency policy.

evidence.claim: Cross-cluster E2E synchronization latency (Table 2a, Qwen3-30B-A3B, derived as T_same,disk + T_upload,p50 + T_download,p50 over Alibaba OSS, Zstd-compressed, bandwidth 0.1/1/10 Gbps): AReaL-DTE 477.47/71.31/30.70 s on GSM8K vs ByteCheckpoint 8741.18/1080.12/314.05 s and PULSE 544.86/140.90/99.43 s. Speedups up to 19.9x over ByteCheckpoint and 3.2x over PULSE (the PULSE gap widens with bandwidth, reaching 3.2x at 10 Gbps).
evidence.value: Qwen3-30B-A3B GSM8K: 477.47/71.31/30.70 s (0.1/1/10 Gbps); up to 19.9x vs ByteCheckpoint, 3.2x vs PULSE
evidence.baseline: ByteCheckpoint (dense complete-state checkpoint); PULSE (sparse changed-values but retains previous checkpoint)
evidence.condition: Qwen3-30B-A3B, 16 H200 GPUs, storage-mediated cross-cluster, Alibaba OSS, Zstd, 0.1/1/10 Gbps

evidence.claim: Same-cluster E2E synchronization latency (Table 3, Qwen3-8B): AReaL-DTE synchronizes Qwen3-8B in 2.77-2.87 s, yielding speedups up to 7.6x over ByteCheckpoint-NCCL and 7.4x over PULSE-NCCL; benefit comes from constructing receiver-specific sparse updates and applying them directly to destination shards. (Abstract reports up to 7.6x and 7.4x within a cluster.)
evidence.value: Qwen3-8B same-cluster 2.77-2.87 s; up to 7.6x vs ByteCheckpoint-NCCL, 7.4x vs PULSE-NCCL
evidence.baseline: ByteCheckpoint-NCCL; PULSE-NCCL (direct NCCL and disk-mediated variants)
evidence.condition: Qwen3-8B, 8 H200 GPUs, same high-bandwidth cluster, AReaL-DTE direct sparse point-to-point path

evidence.claim: Transferred data volume: on Qwen3-30B-A3B AReaL-DTE produces Zstd-compressed sparse files of only 2.53-2.87 GB vs ~44.5 GB for ByteCheckpoint's compressed dense files (16.3x smaller on average), even though <2% of weights change, because every sparse entry stores both an int32 index and a BF16 value. On Qwen3-8B, AReaL-DTE reduces average Zstd-compressed artifact size by 19.7x relative to ByteCheckpoint.
evidence.value: Qwen3-30B-A3B sparse 2.53-2.87 GB vs dense ~44.5 GB (16.3x smaller); Qwen3-8B 19.7x smaller vs ByteCheckpoint; <2% weights change
evidence.condition: Zstd compression, <2% BF16 weight elements change between consecutive policy versions

evidence.claim: Peak memory (Table 2b, Qwen3-30B-A3B cross-cluster): AReaL-DTE GPU 71.52-71.96 GB / CPU 37.44-40.75 GB vs ByteCheckpoint GPU ~121 GB / CPU ~121-125 GB and PULSE GPU ~128-129 GB / CPU ~138-140 GB. AReaL-DTE reduces peak GPU memory by at least 40% and peak CPU memory by at least 66% relative to storage-mediated baselines (abstract reports ~41% GPU / >=87% CPU in same-cluster Qwen3-30B-A3B). Same-cluster Qwen3-8B peak CPU memory 3.45-3.48 GB vs 34.08-34.16 GB (ByteCheckpoint-NCCL) and 36.09-36.53 GB (PULSE-NCCL).
evidence.value: Qwen3-30B-A3B GPU ~71 GB vs ~121/~128 GB; CPU ~37-40 GB vs ~121-125/~138-140 GB; >=40% GPU, >=66% CPU reduction (cross-cluster); same-cluster Qwen3-8B CPU 3.45-3.48 GB
evidence.condition: Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-8B, H200 GPUs, peak memory during construction/staging/communication/application
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 11 (Table 2b); PDF Page 12 (Section 5.3, 5.4); PDF Page 13 (same-cluster Qwen3-8B CPU)

evidence.claim: Training-loop overhead (Figure 4, normalized as T_weight_sync / T_step_without_weight): at 10 Gbps AReaL-DTE overhead is 0.68-0.99x the policy-training time across the four workloads (Qwen3-30B-A3B 0.92-0.99x; Qwen3-8B 0.68-0.99x), whereas ByteCheckpoint and PULSE still incur 5.75-6.56x and 2.14-2.37x respectively. AReaL-DTE reduces weight synchronization from a dominant bottleneck to a cost comparable to or lower than the remaining training step.
evidence.value: at 10 Gbps AReaL-DTE 0.68-0.99x training time vs ByteCheckpoint 5.75-6.56x and PULSE 2.14-2.37x
evidence.condition: cross-cluster, 10 Gbps, normalized to training-step time excluding weight sync

evaluation_context: Hardware: NVIDIA H200 GPUs; Qwen3-8B uses 8 GPUs, Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) uses 16 GPUs. Models span dense (Qwen3-8B) and mixture-of-experts (Qwen3-30B-A3B) architectures. Workloads: four online RL datasets (GSM8K, HumanEval, MATH-500, LogiQA). Deployment: same-cluster (one high-bandwidth cluster, AReaL-DTE direct sparse point-to-point; baselines use direct NCCL and disk-mediated variants) and cross-cluster (training and rollout workers do not share an NCCL group; all methods use storage-mediated paths via Alibaba Cloud OSS with Zstd compression; effective inter-cluster bandwidths 0.1/1/10 Gbps). Cross-cluster latency is DERIVED as T_same,disk + T_upload,p50(B) + T_download,p50(B) (median storage-transfer times), not a direct end-to-end measurement. Baselines: ByteCheckpoint (dense complete-state checkpoint, parallelism-independent representation, load-time remapping) and PULSE (transfers changed BF16 values but retains previous checkpoint). Metrics: E2E synchronization latency (construction+communication+application for same-cluster; derived for cross-cluster) and peak GPU/CPU memory during construction/staging/communication/application.
limitations: The cross-cluster E2E latency is a DERIVED metric (T_same,disk + median upload + median download over OSS), not a direct end-to-end measurement of a real cross-cluster run; p50 storage-transfer times hide tail behavior and OSS-specific dynamics. Only two baselines (ByteCheckpoint, PULSE) are compared; other relevant systems (TensorHub reference-oriented transfer, ROSE shard/sparsity-aware transfer, DORA multi-version, Laminar relay workers, Weave) are discussed as related work but not benchmarked. RL correctness/staleness impact is out of scope: AReaL-DTE optimizes the data-plane synchronization operation, not the rollout schedule, RL algorithm, or consistency policy, so any effect of sparse/asynchronous publication on training convergence is not measured here. Evaluation is limited to two Qwen3 models and four math/code/QA RL datasets; other model families and non-RL workloads are not covered. The <2% changed-weight fraction is workload-dependent and may not hold for other RL algorithms or training regimes. Absolute synchronization latency at 10 Gbps still equals 0.68-0.99x of the training step, so weight sync remains a non-trivial fraction of the loop even with AReaL-DTE.
project_relevance: Relevant to the cross-region card's question of how compression, incremental/delta transfer, and placement reduce bandwidth and latency for moving large model/cache state across clusters: AReaL-DTE is a concrete snapshot-free delta-transfer engine that exploits <2% per-step weight sparsity to cut transferred volume 16.3x-19.7x (Zstd-compressed sparse vs dense) and cut cross-cluster sync latency up to 19.9x (vs ByteCheckpoint) / 3.2x (vs PULSE) at 10 Gbps, reducing weight-sync overhead to <=the training-step time. The on-demand AdamW-inversion reconstruction (avoiding a persistent historical snapshot) and receiver-local coordinate remapping are concrete instances of the card's 'incremental transfer + placement' levers for bridging heterogeneous layouts. Caveat for project use: the cross-cluster number is a derived metric over OSS, not a direct WAN measurement, and the workload is policy-weight sync for RL post-training rather than KV-cache or agent-cache transfer; nonetheless it is a directly relevant technique for making frequent cross-cluster state publication cheap.
